title: A `throw` inside a `finally` block discards the error in flight.
text: `try { throw new IOError("first"); } finally { throw new LogicError("second"); }` compiles, and the handler outside sees only the `LogicError`, with `previous` set to `null`. The `IOError` is lost with no `catch` anywhere. `rule:statements/no-return-leaves-a-finally` refuses `return`, `break` and `continue` there because they would discard a throw in flight, and calls that the one way an exception could vanish without a handler, so the rule and the binary disagree. A call in the `finally` that throws does the same. It closes when the rule decides the case (a diagnostic for a direct `throw`, or the new error carrying the one in flight), with a conformance case.
